full_judgment: 20. When a simple thing could be stated simply and when such thing has been stated previously it is incomprehensible as to why the draftsman had created a smokescreen thereby putting a Legislative intention a subject matter of speculation. If from order against the acquittal an appeal was to be given it could be stated clearly as it was done in the P.O. 50. The Appellate Tribunal may confirm, set aside and enhance, vary, modify any judgment or order. If it is the case that `judgment' includes acquittal as well then the appellate Court may set aside no doubt but then where is the power for infliction of sentence after "finding him guilty and pass sentence" as required by section 423 Cr. P.C. It will not be suggested that those words have been used superfluously and they are redundant. Nor can it be suggested that the finding of guilt is concomitant feature of reversal of acquittal. Though the. Code makes no distinction between an appeal from an acquittal and one from conviction, yet certain well-settled principles over the few decades have found favour with all the High Courts in the subcontinent. One of these is that every than is to be presumed innocent until his guilt is established. Another is that of reasonable doubt the accused must have the benefit of that doubt. An appellant from conviction can always invoke the support of these principles, if he can show that the facts of his case come within their purview. On the other hand, the tale of the appellant from a judgment of acquittal is more difficult to satisfy the Court that the accosted can derive no benefit from them on the facts of the case under appeal.
